sessions.note: Model extracted from the banked score-29 candidate; simulate matches the dump 20/23. The three mismatches (pseudos 100/106/112, all $t-registers) are the documented reload spill-retry divergence - this function is the ra_solver README's known case. All three $s-register roles match exactly (78 = b -> $s2, 82 = yoff -> $s3, 79 = outer -> $s4), so the part that matters is faithful. PERTURB (spec {78:19, 82:20, 79:18}), 200 single atoms: exactly three hits, all priority lifts on pseudo 79 - refs+1, refs+2, live-8. NO conflict, preference or birth-order atom reaches the target. That closes the team-lead's hypothesis that the solver's non-priority atoms might be the missing model for this function: the round-10 priority framing was right and is now proven exhaustive at single-atom depth. ROUTE 1 VALIDATED END-TO-END for the first time: a probe realizing refs+1 (yoff = outer - 1 in the else arm, run as a DIAGNOSTIC not a candidate) lifts pseudo 79 from pri 2000 to 2400 and produces exactly the target rotation (b->$s3, yoff->$s4, outer->$s2), moving the honest score 29 -> 18 - the first movement since round 7. REJECTED as a candidate on two independent grounds: it is a coercion (the value is the constant 0 spelled through a variable that happens to hold 1, no semantic purpose, justification reaches into the allocator), and it emits addiu s4,s2,-1 where TARGET EMITS move s4,zero - provably not the original's code, so it can never reach 0 by that route. ROUTE 2 IS NEW (tmp/ra/stf_whatif.py), a 2-atom solution the single-atom search misses: b livelen ~75 AND yoff livelen ~55 together also give the target rotation. Not spellable either - staging b from the parameter lengthens it but ADDS references (nrefs 7->9, pri 4500), moving priority the wrong way, and yoff cannot be lengthened without a def since both its defs are inside the guard arms. DECISIVE NEW EVIDENCE: neither route is what the original did. Target references outer at exactly the same four sites we do - move s2,zero (65), bnez s2 (66), addiu s2,s2,1 (112), slti v0,s2,2 (113) - i.e. the same nrefs and the same span, hence the same priority 2000. The original therefore reached the rotation with no priority difference at all. Combined with this being the one function whose dump carries reload-retry effects, the likeliest explanation is that its final allocation is decided post-reload, outside the modeled path. SECOND CLUSTER REVEALED: with the rotation fixed (score 18) the remaining diffs are a different group - the gpu_LoadImage argument setup (target addiu a0,sp,24 / lui a1 / addu a1,v0,a1 where ours uses $t0), plus sll v0,s1,0x5 vs sll a1,s1,0x5 and li t0,1 vs li v1,1 - precisely pseudos 100/106/112, the reload-retry trio. So the rotation is worth about 11 points and closing it alone does NOT reach 0. Other new negatives: guard inversion is byte-identical; a reference to outer outside the arms (idx = outer - outer) folds away, confirming duplicated-statement-into-arms cannot supply the sixth reference because the arms are guarded by outer == 0. src/text1a.c reverted.

sessions.lever: else-arm round: the refs+1 route is CLOSED by a measured fold/emit dichotomy. Foldable outer-expressions are never born (5 refs in the FIRST .rtl dump); unfoldable ones cost exactly one instruction target does not have. Target has only 4 instructions touching outer's register, carrying all 5 existing refs - there is no byte-neutral home for a 6th. Best probe (xoff = 0x7F + outer) gives the exact rotation and 29 -> 18 but is one insn off.
sessions.note: Followed up the validated refs+1 route with the team-lead's else-arm insight, which is correct in one respect: round 10's "references fold before reg_n_refs" result WAS measured in the then arm, and in the else arm GCC 2.7.2 does not derive outer == 1 from a two-pass loop, so a reference there is genuinely unfoldable. That turns out to be exactly why the route cannot close. MEASURED DICHOTOMY (tmp/ra/prio.sh for nrefs, tmp/ra/passcensus.sh for the per-pass census). Foldable else-arm spellings - yoff = outer & 0, outer * 0, outer - outer - leave nrefs at 5 and pri at 2000, no rotation, bytes unchanged. Unfoldable ones - xoff = 0x7F + outer, xoff = 0x80 * outer - give nrefs 6, pri 2400, and EXACTLY the target rotation (b->$s3, yoff->$s4, outer->$s2), score 29 -> 18, but each costs exactly one instruction target does not have. The best of them, xoff = 0x7F + outer (S_E5), is strictly better than the earlier yoff = outer - 1 probe: the whole arm region matches target INCLUDING move s4,zero, and the only divergence in the window is li s5,128 becoming addiu s5,s2,127. WHY THE PROBES ARE REJECTED, stated explicitly per the team-lead's request: they are not dead stores and they do not change semantics on the executed path; they are rejected because (a) each is a coercion, a constant spelled through a variable that happens to hold 1, and (b) each CHANGES THE BYTES - it emits an instruction target does not have. WHICH PASS EATS EACH ATTEMPT: none does. The pass census counts pseudo-79 appearances in every -da dump from .rtl through .lreg. For outer & 0 the count is 5 in the VERY FIRST .rtl dump, identical to baseline - the fold happens in the front end before RTL expansion, so the reference is never born rather than being eaten later. For xoff = 0x7F + outer the count is 6 from .rtl all the way through .lreg. So in GCC 2.7.2 a reference and an instruction are the same object: there is no window in which a ref exists without its insn, which is what a byte-neutral ref-lift would require. STRUCTURAL CLOSER: target has nowhere to put a sixth reference. Its only instructions touching outer's register in the loop region are move s2,zero (65), bnez s2 (66), addiu s2,s2,1 (112) and slti v0,s2,2 (113) - four instructions carrying exactly the five refs we already have. The sw / move s2,a2 / sll / lw at 6, 7, 40 and 130 belong to the blue-channel value that shares the register earlier. A byte-neutral sixth reference would need a fifth $s2 instruction that does not exist. Byte-neutrality and the extra reference are mutually exclusive. DUPLICATED-STATEMENT FAMILY, else arm included: a real 0xF0 * (outer +/- 1) statement duplicated into BOTH arms gives nrefs 7 and pri 2641 but the WRONG permutation (b->$s4, yoff->$s3, outer->$s2), and it perturbs b's livelen from 60 to 63. Not target. src/text1a.c reverted.
